title: One Deflate compressor per authored save instead of one per member
decision: retained, implemented at both Office write sites; the cross-member compressor pool proposed for the preservation writer was implemented, measured and removed
code_state: crates/soapberry-zip only: src/writer.rs, src/office.rs, src/preserve.rs, tests/deflate_reuse.rs
implements: SAVE-4 of change 0587, at the two sites change 0607 identified
reason_codes: the streaming archive writer behind every authored XLSX, DOCX and PPTX publication constructed one flate2 DeflateEncoder per member, 161 per 50-slide authored PPTX save, each allocating and zeroing a ~300 KiB compressor state; it now drives change 0476's reusable state, one per archive
the reset moved from the end of a member to the start of the next one, so a save with a single Deflate member pays exactly the one construction it always paid and no reset at all

the preservation writer keeps one compressor per regenerated member, but builds it as a ReusableDeflateState driven by ReusedDeflateEncoder, which removes flate2's per-codec-call zeroing of its output vector's spare capacity

carrying one compressor across a preservation plan's regenerated members reached 40 constructions -> 1 and callgrind Ir -42.74%, but cost +14.1% native cycles, +9.9% instructions and 271 minor page faults per publish, and was removed
the one-entry mini-archive round trip in the preservation writer was priced at 617 Ir per member (0.15% of a regenerated member) and deliberately left in place

accepted_evidence.byte_identity: 336 OOXML fixtures x 4 mutation scenarios (1,344 rows) and x 3 multi-member regeneration scenarios (1,008 rows), published length and SHA-256 or typed error, empty diff on both; 422 editor-route rows from tabs, edit_cells and append_plain_paragraph over the whole corpus (110 digests, 312 typed refusals), empty diff; 48 authored-PPTX digests across six deck sizes, empty diff; 78 opened decks, exact-source passthrough 78 of 78 on both legs
accepted_evidence.counts: callgrind isolation pairs for five scenarios on both legs, with per-save Deflate-compressor construction and reset counts; per-caller attribution of memset and memcpy behind the rejected variant
accepted_evidence.native: perf stat -x, -r 5 isolation pairs for cycles, instructions and minor page faults on five scenarios, both legs
accepted_evidence.timing: paired A1 B1 B2 A2 timing with an A/A floor in the same window: the authored 50-slide save (40 samples per leg-run) and the preservation publish at 40 and at 1 regenerated member (2,000 samples per leg-run, two windows each)
accepted_evidence.tests: four differentials in tests/deflate_reuse.rs requiring complete ZIP-byte equality with one fresh DeflateEncoder per member, including the member that follows a refused one; one unit test in preserve.rs comparing a regenerated member's framing, payload and central record against a fresh flate2 mini archive over six payload sizes
accepted_evidence.gates: seven sections, all exit 0: fmt, clippy, test and doc for soapberry-zip (593 tests), plus the consumer suites litchi-opc (675), litchi-xlsx/litchi-docx/litchi-pptx (340) and litchi-odt/litchi-odc/litchi-odf-common/litchi-iwa-archive (352)

accepted_costs.callgrind_over_pricing: callgrind counts rep stos once per byte and the compressor's ~300 KiB state zeroing is exactly that, so its -42.85% and -38.64% instruction deltas are an upper bound; the native cycle deltas (-12.24% and -13.92%) are the price
accepted_costs.host_contention: seven other agents were building and measuring on the host; run-window load average 20-25, and both timing windows carry their own A/A floor
accepted_costs.tail_statistics: the p99 delta on the authored save is inside the A/A floor (-14.36%) and is not claimed; window 1 of the preservation timing carries a tail outlier in its A1 leg, so only window 2's tail is read
accepted_costs.allocator_dependence: the page-fault mechanism that sank the pooled variant is glibc-malloc behaviour; a different allocator could rank it differently

known_gaps.not_measured: authored DOCX and XLSX publication uses the same writer and the same code path but was covered only by the byte-identity oracles and the test suites, not by its own timing, because tools/perf-baseline still has no ordinary-save selector
known_gaps.corpora: every regenerated member in the preservation scenarios is a .rels part of a few hundred bytes, so those numbers are the fixed per-member cost and not a payload-size result; no fixture in the corpus regenerates a large content part through the preservation writer
known_gaps.environment: cold cache, physical devices, peak RSS, allocation profiles, non-glibc allocators and non-Linux platforms were not measured

withheld: any p99 claim on the authored save
any claim at all for a preservation publish with a single regenerated member
any cold-cache, real-device, peak-RSS, allocation-profile or cross-platform result
